newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-British Land to build profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-British Land to build profits.

text.p: British property company British Land Co Plc is expected to report increased pre-tax profits when it reports its results for the year to the end of March next Wednesday, analysts said on Friday.
"We're expecting a pretty confident trading statement," one property analyst told Reuters, adding this was likely to show improvement in both rental and investment values.
Analysts predict pre-tax profits for the period to total between 75 and 79 million stg, up from 65.7 million stg the previous year.
They forecast earnings per share of between 11.9 and 12.5 pence a share and a dividend of nine pence.
Forecasts for British Land's net asset value (NAV) vary from 471 pence to 503 pence, compared with 426 pence at the end of 1995/96.
But confidence could be tempered by "a slight cautionary statement" on the dangers of the British property market, which is showing signs of increasing buoyancy, the analyst said.
British Land, which last month launched a 300 million stg 10-year convertible bond, has several development schemes in the pipeline.

Analysts said they are keen to know how much of its London Corn Exchange development has been let, whether it intends proceeding with further phases of an office scheme in central London's Euston Road and the start date for its Plantation House redevelopment in the City.
